session_cue.text: Father William measuring Uriah's hands and feet with a ruler

previous.text: Dunk found a glowing magical mithril chain shirt in Warwick's shop and said he had a plan to get it.
Trout and Dr. Uriah used ink to catch the invisible Clurichen, Naggeneen, and Quinn hung him behind the bar.
Dunk struck a deal with Ingrid to put Warwick to sleep with a potion. He secretly diluted the faun wine he gave her.
Father William, the town priest, measured Dr. Uriah's hands and feet for webbing and found none.
Father William marked the witch's home and Brandon's Barrow Mound on Dr. Uriah's map.
George told the party the dragon's lair lies north at the foot of the mountains.
Trout recruited Squints as a junior assistant in his Halfling Corps.
Dunk astonished the fauns by drinking their wine unaffected, then traded a child's rabbit's foot for a flask.
Dr. Uriah bonded with Ingrid over disliking Father William, and she said hidden fairies are appearing more often.
Led by Trout, the party set out for Brandon's Barrow Mound and told Dunk to meet them there.
Squints pulled a bound Brother Dirk from the giant's sack, and the party outran the waking giant.

current.where_you_are: The party is in the forest north of town, across the field from the giant's stone cottage. Squints and the freed Brother Dirk are with them.

immediate_intention.text: The party is walking to the Barrow to get the sword. They are pressing Brother Dirk to come along instead of going home, and Trout has told Dirk he will report to Squints. Dirk has not answered yet.

Your goals.text: Find the treasure marked on the party's treasure map.
Kill the black dragon and drag its body into Brandonsford to collect Eric the Reeve's 1000 gold.
Get Warwick the smith's magical mithril chain shirt.

Standing in your way.text: George says arrows and swords could not pierce the dragon's black scales.

What could help.text: If the party helps Ingrid give Warwick her sleeping potion, Dunk can search his home for the mithril shirt unnoticed. The potion isn't finished, and the diluted faun wine may weaken it.
Father William says the dragon can't be killed without the magic sword buried at Brandon's Barrow Mound. George says no one knows if the legend is true.
The party plans to check one of the map's marked locations on the way to Brandon's Barrow Mound.
Drop Dead Ned, a murderous thief, offers to join the party for 100 gold a week if he gets to kill people. Dr. Uriah is thinking it over.
Warwick sleeps in the second-story bedroom of his shop, and its window is left cracked open.
If the party gets Warwick's mithril chain shirt, it could protect them against the dragon.
If the party hires Lady Hilda, a seasoned fighter staying at the Clumsy Fox, she will join the dragon hunt.
George says a lance may be one of the few weapons not yet tried on the dragon. Sir Phidipaldi plans to bring his.

Still unanswered.text: Where are the treasure map's marked locations, and which holds the treasure?
Why have shipments stopped reaching Brandonsford?

Promises and debts.text: Dunk agreed to help Ingrid give the sleeping potion to Warwick.
The party must give Squints second pick of its first treasure, after the Halfling Corps' elite members.
Dr. Uriah must give penance at Brandon's Barrow Mound, as Father William asked.

Meanwhile.text: George says the black dragon killed all his friends when they attacked its lair. Its bite is deadly poison, and it spits sulfur.
George warns the dragon cannot fly yet but soon will, and says that then they are all doomed.
The giant that captured Brother Dirk to eat still lives on the party's route north, though it is slow.

threads.name: The treasure map
threads.note: Dr. Uriah still carries the map and plans to copy it, Father William added the witch's home and the Barrow Mound to it, and the party plans to check a marked location on the way to the Barrow. The treasure is still unfound.

threads.name: The Brandonsford dragon
threads.note: George answered where the lair is and warned the dragon will soon fly (beat_63). Father William and George established that it reportedly can only be killed with Brandon's sword (beat_54, beat_66), which changes the shape of the hunt. The dragon and the reward remain open.

threads.name: The Clurichen
threads.note: The Clurichen Naggeneen was caught and revealed as a drinker who empties bars (beat_20, beat_21), so the question is answered and the nightly threat ended. He still hangs captive in a bag behind Quinn's bar (beat_26), and his offer of a pot of gold or a secret for release remains.

threads.name: Lady Hilda's offer to join the hunt
threads.note: Lady Hilda was only seen dining. Sir Phidipaldi's promise to come back and hire her is unreleased.

threads.name: Brandonsford's missing shipments
threads.note: Shipments still had not come in the next morning, and the cause is unknown.

threads.name: Drop Dead Ned's offer
threads.note: Ned was only seen at the tavern, and his offer stands unanswered.

threads.name: Shamus the mule
threads.note: Dunk offered 20 gold, and Gill said he would go lower than 100 only once his sons return (beat_3), renegotiating the terms.

threads.name: Quinn's fake shipment scheme
threads.note: The bar thief was caught (beat_20, beat_23) and Quinn paid the reward of 33 gold each (beat_25), so nothing remains open.

threads.name: Squints and the Halfling Corps
threads.note: Trout recruited Squints on stated terms, including second pick after the first treasure (beat_42), and later put Brother Dirk under him (beat_90). Those terms remain live, as does Trout's secret plan not to rescue him.

threads.name: Warwick's mithril chain shirt
threads.note: Dunk found a glowing magical mithril shirt in Warwick's shop and says he has a plan to get it (beat_46). It might help against the dragon, but no purpose was stated that makes it a child of the hunt.

threads.name: Ingrid's sleeping potion
threads.note: Dunk and Ingrid arranged a sleeping potion for Warwick. Dunk fetched and diluted the faun wine and handed it over (beat_72, beat_78), and Ingrid is now brewing it with a meeting set for tonight (beat_79). Her secret, which Dunk holds over her (beat_38), is part of this one bargain.

threads.name: Brandon's sword at the Barrow
threads.note: Father William states the dragon can't be killed without the sword buried with Brandon (beat_54), giving the trip a stated purpose under the hunt. The party set out to get it (beat_51).

threads.name: Uriah's penance for Father William
threads.note: Dr. Uriah promised penance at the Barrow Mound and a 10 gold donation. Neither has been done yet.

threads.name: The giant in the woods
threads.note: The party robbed the giant of its captive and fled, but the giant still lives in its cottage on the route north. Escaping did not end the danger.

facts.text: Find the treasure marked on the party's treasure map.

Dr. Uriah carries the party's treasure map, which marks several unrecognized locations around Brandonsford where the party assumes the treasure lies; Father William has added the witch's home and the Barrow Mound to it.

classification.support_basis: The map is the party's only guide to the treasure, though its original marked locations are still unidentified.

facts.resource_subject: The party's map carried by Dr. Uriah, now marking the witch's home and the Barrow

facts.text: Where are the locations marked on the treasure map, and which one holds the treasure?

classification.question_basis: The map marks several locations the party doesn't recognize; identifying them is what the party must discover to find the treasure, a live adventure-level want.
classification.grounding_justification: The marked locations are explicitly unrecognized and the treasure's spot is only assumed.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Mostly a matter of locating places, though which one holds treasure is uncertain.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly instrumental toward finding the treasure.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Could be pursued by asking locals and exploring the marked sites.

facts.text: The party plans to check out one of the map's marked locations on the way to Brandon's Barrow Mound.

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: visiting the marked location en route to the Barrow. Benefit: learning whether that site holds the treasure, narrowing the search. Beat_51 records the agreed plan.
classification.support_basis: Investigating a marked site directly tests one of the map's possible treasure locations, though it is uncertain the treasure is there.
classification.action_basis: The party agreed to check the marked location on its route through the forest to the Barrow; the map shows the site.

facts.text: Where did the party's treasure map come from?

classification.question_basis: Beat_4 notes Dr. Uriah could recall nothing of the map's history; this is a background gap rather than something the treasure hunt requires.
classification.grounding_justification: The beat notes the history is unremembered, but play does not frame it as a mystery.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer might explain who made the map, but nothing suggests a hidden situation.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mildly interesting background with no established significance.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: No leads or sources about the map's origin have been established.

facts.text: Kill the black dragon near Brandonsford and drag its body into town to collect Eric the Reeve's 1000 gold.

Eric the Reeve says the woodsman George, who met the dragon and lost an arm to it, lives a couple of houses down and may come to the Clumsy Fox tonight; the party could question him about where and how he encountered it.
facts.ended_how: used up: Sir Phidipaldi questioned George at his hut

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: seeking out George at his house or the tavern. Benefit: first-hand knowledge of where the dragon was met and what it is like, helping the party find it.
classification.support_basis: George is the only named witness who fought the dragon, so his account could point the party toward it.
classification.action_basis: Eric pointed the party to George as a source and said where he lives.

facts.text: Where can the black dragon be found?
facts.ended_how: answered: George says its lair is north at the foot of the mountains (replaced by fact_new_1)

classification.question_basis: The dragon's whereabouts were unknown; finding it is essential to killing it for the bounty.
classification.grounding_justification: Rumors and encounters established a dragon whose whereabouts were unknown.

facts.text: George says the black dragon killed all his friends when they attacked its lair: its poisoned bite kills, it spits sulfur, and it may kill those who confront it.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: George describes a lethal poison bite and his friends' deaths.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: Death of those who attack it.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: First-hand testimony from George, who lost his arm and friends.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: The party is heading toward confronting it; past attack on its lair killed everyone but George.
classification.preventability_justification: The party can prepare, seek the sword or armor, or choose how to approach.

facts.classification_change_basis: Beat_64 establishes the bite is lethal and the dragon killed George's friends, raising severity from maiming to death.

facts.text: What will become of Farmer Gill's three sons, who are out trying to kill the dragon now?

classification.question_basis: Gill's sons are hunting the dragon; their outcome is an open circumstance of the hunt, not a central investigative objective.
classification.grounding_justification: Stated they are hunting it, leaving the outcome open.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Little beyond asking Gill or finding the sons.

facts.text: Lady Hilda's offer to join the hunt for pay (thread_4) could add a seasoned fighter against the dragon.

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: hiring Lady Hilda. Benefit: an armored, seasoned fighter making the dragon kill easier.
classification.support_basis: She looks more seasoned than the party and offered to hunt the dragon with them.
classification.action_basis: Hilda explicitly offered to join adventurers hunting the dragon for money.

facts.text: George says the dragon's lair is north at the foot of the mountains, reachable without climbing.

classification.support_basis: Tells the party where to go to confront the dragon, resting on George's first-hand experience.

facts.text: George warns the dragon cannot fly yet but soon will, and says that then they are all doomed.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: A flying dragon dooming the area is suggested but the specific harm is vague.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: Doom for the town and region affects many.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: George's testimony from encountering it; not observed by the party.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: George says it will fly soon, an advancing process, but no timeline.
classification.preventability_justification: Killing the dragon before it flies would prevent it, though the means are uncertain.

facts.text: George says arrows and swords could not pierce the dragon's black scales.

classification.scope_basis: The scales are a lasting property of the dragon that stops ordinary weapons from killing it.

facts.text: Getting Brandon's magic sword from the Barrow (thread_12) could let the party kill the dragon; Father William says it can't be killed without it.

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: retrieving the sword from Brandon's Barrow. Benefit: per Father William and legend, the only weapon able to kill the dragon.
classification.support_basis: Would overcome the dragon's invulnerability, though George says no one knows what is true of the legend.
classification.action_basis: The party decided to walk to the Barrow to get the sword, whose location is known.

facts.resource_subject: Legend that only Brandon's magic sword can kill the dragon

facts.text: Warwick's magical mithril chain shirt (thread_10), which Dunk says he has a plan to get, could protect against the dragon.

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: obtaining Warwick's mithril shirt. Benefit: magical armor protecting a fighter against the dragon's attacks.
classification.support_basis: Armor could reduce risk in the fight, though whether it stops a poison bite is unestablished.
classification.action_basis: Dunk saw the shirt in Warwick's shop and says he has a plan to get it.

facts.text: George allows a lance may be one of the few weapons not yet tried on the dragon; Sir Phidipaldi plans to bring his lance.

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: bringing Sir Phidipaldi's lance against the dragon. Benefit: an untried weapon that might pierce its scales.
classification.support_basis: Only possibly effective; George merely notes it hasn't been tried.
classification.action_basis: Sir Phidipaldi has a lance and said he would bring it.

facts.text: Does Eric the Reeve actually have the 1000 gold he promised for the dragon?

classification.question_basis: George doubts Eric has the reward money; a bounded check on the reward rather than a central investigation.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A single fact about Eric's funds.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Could be checked by asking around or confronting Eric.

facts.text: Reginald the Frog warns that a little trickster creature called a Clurichen comes from the riverbanks into Brandonsford every night, up to no good, and that the party should stay away from wherever it goes.
facts.ended_how: removed: the Clurichen Naggeneen was caught and now hangs captive in a bag behind Quinn's bar (beat_20, beat_24, beat_26)

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: Reginald only says the creature is up to no good and to stay away; no particular harm is named.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: It is described as a little trickster, suggesting mischief rather than serious harm.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: Rests on a single warning from a talking frog, testimony of uncertain reliability.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: Reginald says it comes into town every night, an ongoing pattern, but no harmful progression is shown.
classification.preventability_justification: The party could follow the advice to avoid where it goes, though they do not know where that is.

facts.text: What does the Clurichen do when it comes into town each night?
facts.ended_how: answered: Naggeneen sneaks into the Golden Egg's basement to drink Quinn's alcohol (beat_21, beat_23)

classification.question_basis: Reginald's warning that the creature enters town nightly up to no good, without saying what it does, raises the question; no adventure want depends on it, so it is a possible revelation rather than an objective.
classification.grounding_justification: A specific warning about nightly mischief clearly raises what the creature does.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal a hidden nightly activity and its intent.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Play has not tied the creature to other events, so the answer is mainly mildly interesting.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: The party could watch the riverbanks or town at night or question Reginald and townsfolk.

facts.text: Naggeneen, hung captive in a bag behind Quinn's bar, offers his pot of gold or a secret to whoever lets him go; Quinn holds him, and Sir Phidipaldi refused the offer on grounds of honor.

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: releasing Naggeneen from Quinn's bag. Benefit: a pot of gold or an unspecified secret, which play links to no want or debt of the party.
classification.support_basis: No established want or debt is served by the gold or the unnamed secret, and releasing him would mean taking him from Quinn's custody.
classification.action_basis: Naggeneen did offer these terms, but no concrete advantage toward any party want is established and release would require going against Quinn.

facts.resource_subject: Naggeneen captive in a bag behind Quinn's bar and his offer for release

facts.text: What does Quinn intend to do with the captive Naggeneen?

classification.question_basis: Quinn said he knew what he would do with Naggeneen and hung the bag behind his bar without saying more; no party want depends on it, so it is an ordinary gap.
classification.grounding_justification: Quinn's pointed remark clearly raises the question.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: One answer from Quinn or one observation would settle it.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mildly interesting, with no wider connections established.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: The party could simply ask Quinn.

facts.text: Lady Hilda, a seasoned fighter in chain mail and shield, would join the party for pay to hunt the dragon, which she can't hunt alone.

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: the party returns to the Clumsy Fox and hires Lady Hilda for money. Benefit: a seasoned, armored fighter joins the dragon hunt, strengthening the party against the dragon. She was still dining at the Clumsy Fox this Session (beat_40) and has not withdrawn the offer.
classification.support_basis: She looks more seasoned than the party and is armored, adding real fighting strength to the hunt for the Reeve's bounty; her fee is not yet set.
classification.action_basis: Lady Hilda explicitly said she would join a party of adventurers hunting the dragon for money, and she remains in town at the Clumsy Fox.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi told Lady Hilda the party would talk to the Reeve and come back to hire her.

classification.stake_basis: Only a stated plan to return and hire her; no evidence Lady Hilda relies on or has a claim to the party coming back.

facts.text: Why have shipments stopped reaching Brandonsford? Bentley's tavern restock is a week overdue, and Farmer Gill says nothing has come into town in months.

classification.question_basis: Two independent sources described the town being cut off with no cause given, and this Session shipments still had not come in the next morning. Answering it would reveal a hidden circumstance affecting the whole town. No party want to restore the shipments is established, so it is a revelation question rather than an adventure objective.
classification.grounding_justification: Townsfolk independently state that shipments have stopped, and they still had not arrived this Session, clearly raising the question of why.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal an underlying cause cutting off a whole town's supply, possibly tied to other local troubles.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Learning what stops the supply would explain the town's hardship and change the party's understanding of Brandonsford.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: It could be pursued by questioning merchants, tracing supply routes and examining the roads into town.

facts.text: Drop Dead Ned, a murderous thief with a killer wasp in a jar, offers to hire on with the party for 100 gold a week, willing to do anything as long as he gets to kill people; Dr. Uriah said he'd think about it.

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: hiring Ned at 100 gold a week. Benefit: an extra killer and his killer wasp as fighting strength, matching the established dragon hunt with the Reeve's 1000 gold bounty.
classification.support_basis: Adds a willing killer and a wasp for fast kills to a party hunting a dragon, though his skill against a dragon is unproven and his only motive is killing people.
classification.action_basis: Ned explicitly offered himself and his wasp for hire on stated terms; combat help is a straightforward capability-to-need match for killing the dragon, and he was still in town at the Clumsy Fox this Session.

facts.text: Get Farmer Gill's mule Shamus.
Farmer Gill would accept work in place of the 100 gold for Shamus, and says the big work he needs is killing the dragon.

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: killing the dragon as work for Gill; benefit: Gill gives Dunk the mule without the 100 gold. This is simply meeting Gill's alternative terms for the very mule wanted.
classification.support_basis: It offers a way to get Shamus without paying 100 gold, though killing the dragon is a large undertaking.
classification.action_basis: Gill answered Dunk's request to trade work by naming killing the dragon as the work he needs.

facts.text: Farmer Gill refused Dunk's 20 gold offer for Shamus and won't go below 100 gold until his sons come back, since without them or the mule he can't get work done.

classification.scope_basis: Gill ties any lower price to his sons' return, a standing condition lasting until they come home, not just this conversation.

facts.text: Catch whoever empties the Golden Egg's bar at night, which Quinn blames on Bentley, and collect Quinn's 100 gold.
facts.ended_how: achieved: the Clurichen Naggeneen was caught in the basement and Quinn paid Sir Phidipaldi, Trout and Dr. Uriah 33 gold each

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi and Quinn agreed a plan: Quinn brings bottles, they fill them with water, and Sir Phidipaldi makes a big show of delivering ale to the Golden Egg to lure whoever empties the bar.
facts.ended_how: obsolete: the thief was caught by other means (the marble trap and ink), so the fake delivery is no longer needed

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: staging the fake ale delivery with Quinn's water-filled bottles. Benefit: baiting the nightly thief into showing itself so it can be caught, which Quinn and Sir Phidipaldi agreed earlier.
classification.support_basis: It gave the party a concrete bait to draw out the culprit, though whether anyone would take the bait was untested.
classification.action_basis: Quinn proposed and Sir Phidipaldi agreed to the plan, with Quinn supplying the bottles.

facts.text: Who or what empties and knocks over the Golden Egg's stock every night? Quinn blames Bentley.
facts.ended_how: answered: the thief was the Clurichen Naggeneen, not Bentley

classification.question_basis: Quinn reported his bar half emptied or knocked over each morning and blamed Bentley only on the basis of the Fox's popularity; the culprit was a genuine hidden truth, but the goal it served is a side job, so it is a revelation rather than an adventure objective.
classification.grounding_justification: Quinn explicitly described the nightly losses and offered a contested explanation, making the culprit conspicuously unresolved.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer reveals a hidden nightly actor and its relationship to the rivalry between the inns.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Learning whether Bentley or something else is responsible changes the party's understanding of Quinn's grievance.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: It supported a staged sting, stakeout and questioning of the tavern owners.

facts.text: Under Trout's recruitment terms, once the party finds its first treasure, Squints gets second pick of it, after the elite members of the Halfling Corps.

classification.stake_basis: Squints agreed to fund himself, bring his own gear, fight monsters and take Trout's orders in exchange for this share. He is new to town and looking for his big break, so he relies on this payoff.

facts.text: Squints, a sling-and-dagger fighter more experienced than Trout, has joined the party as a junior member of the Halfling Corps. He funds himself and takes orders directly from Trout.

classification.support_basis: An extra experienced fighter who has agreed to fight monsters strengthens the party on its dangerous trek through the woods to the Barrow for the sword. He has already proved willing to take risks on Trout's orders.

facts.text: Trout openly promises to intervene if Squints is caught, but he and Sir Phidipaldi have privately agreed not to actually rescue him, so Squints may be left to his fate on a dangerous mission.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: The harm is clear: Squints is abandoned when captured or endangered.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: Being abandoned to a monster could cost Squints his life, though that is harm to one person.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: Trout's whispered statement and Sir Phidipaldi's agreement are recorded directly.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: The stated plan concerned the giant mission, and the party in fact helped him escape; no further mission is set.
classification.preventability_justification: The party controls whether it rescues Squints, so it can simply choose to help.

facts.text: Get Warwick the smith's magical mithril chain shirt, which glows in the moonlight in his shop.
Warwick sleeps in the second-story bedroom of his shop-home, and its window is left cracked open.

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: climbing in through the cracked-open bedroom window. Benefit: entry into the locked shop-home where the mithril shirt is kept, without needing the front door unlocked. Dunk observed the open window while scouting the shirt.
classification.support_basis: It offers a way into the closed shop where the shirt is, though it opens into the room where Warwick sleeps.
classification.action_basis: Dunk saw the open window directly (beat_14); it is a physical opening that needs no one's cooperation.

facts.text: Ingrid's sleeping potion, which Dunk offered to help administer to Warwick, could keep Warwick asleep while Dunk goes after the shirt.

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: administering Ingrid's sleeping potion to Warwick, as Dunk arranged with Ingrid. Benefit: Warwick stays asleep, so Dunk can get to the shirt in his shop-home without being caught.
classification.support_basis: A sleeping Warwick removes the risk of the owner waking; the potion is still being brewed from diluted faun wine, so its strength is unproven.
classification.action_basis: Ingrid agreed to brew the potion and Dunk proposed to help her administer it to Warwick (beat_35, beat_79); keeping the shop's sleeping owner asleep is a straightforward match to taking the shirt.

facts.resource_subject: The sleeping potion Ingrid is brewing

facts.text: Ingrid is brewing a sleeping potion for Warwick from the diluted faun wine Dunk gave her; Dunk plans to see her tonight, though she told him to come back tomorrow. With Warwick drugged asleep, Dunk could enter his house and shop, where the mithril chain shirt is kept.

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: collect the finished potion from Ingrid and administer it to Warwick. Benefit: Warwick stays asleep, removing the risk of him waking while Dunk is inside; Dunk wants the shirt and says he has a plan to get it (beat_46).
classification.support_basis: A sleeping Warwick would let Dunk reach the chain shirt in the house where Warwick sleeps. The potion is not yet finished, and the faun wine was heavily diluted.
classification.action_basis: Ingrid agreed to brew the potion for administering to Warwick and is working on it, and a meeting with Dunk is arranged.

facts.resource_subject: The sleeping potion Ingrid is brewing

facts.text: Dunk agreed to help Ingrid give the sleeping potion to Warwick so she can watch him all night without fear of him waking.

classification.stake_basis: Ingrid is brewing the potion on the strength of Dunk's offer to help administer it, since she cannot reach Warwick's window herself and fears he will wake.

facts.text: Dunk knows Ingrid's secret: she climbs up to Warwick's window every night to watch him sleep and fears being found out. She told Dunk she owes him for keeping it, and he pointedly said he hasn't kept it yet.

classification.support_basis: The leverage helps keep Ingrid cooperating with the potion plan that serves Dunk's pursuit of the chain shirt.

facts.text: Will Ingrid's sleeping potion work, given the heavily diluted faun wine and Father William's claim that she can't make her own potions?

classification.question_basis: Dunk diluted the faun wine to about 20%, and Father William says Ingrid can't make her potions herself, which she denies. This is a practical check on whether an item will work.
classification.grounding_justification: The dilution and the contradicting claims about Ingrid's skill clearly raise doubt.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Using the potion would settle it.

facts.text: Father William says the dragon can't be killed without the magic sword buried with Brandon in Brandon's Barrow Mound, which the party can reach in about a three-mile walk through the forest.

classification.opening_basis: Trigger: walk to the Barrow and recover the sword buried with Brandon. Benefit: per Father William and the legend George tells, it is the weapon that can kill the dragon whose scales arrows and swords could not pierce.
classification.support_basis: It would give the party a way past the dragon's unpierceable scales, though George says no one knows what is true of the legend or where the sword is.
classification.action_basis: The Barrow's location is known and marked, and the party has set out to walk there to get the sword.

facts.resource_subject: Legend that only Brandon's magic sword can kill the dragon

facts.text: Can Brandon's sword really kill the dragon, and is it still at the Barrow?

classification.question_basis: George says only Sir Brandon ever killed the dragon with a fairy-given sword but no one knows what is true or where the sword is, while Father William says it is buried with Brandon; this is a bounded confirmation that will be settled by going to the Barrow.
classification.grounding_justification: George explicitly frames the legend and the sword's whereabouts as uncertain.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: One visit to the Barrow and a test against the dragon would settle it.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Confirming an old legend is mildly interesting but mainly instrumental.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Farmer Gill knows the fairytales, giving a modest lead beyond simply going there.

facts.text: Will Brother Dirk go home as he suggested, or continue toward the Barrow for the sword?

classification.question_basis: After his rescue Dirk said he should just head home, Sir Phidipaldi objected, Uriah raised Father William's expectations, and Dirk's response to Trout was not recorded; play left his course unsettled. It is a routine question about one NPC's next move.
classification.grounding_justification: The scene directly raises whether Dirk will abandon his mission.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: His choice matters for the party but is not a revelation.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Dirk is immediately present to ask.

facts.text: Dr. Uriah agreed, at Father William's request, to give penance at Brandon's Barrow Mound.

classification.stake_basis: Father William specifically asked for this penance and Uriah agreed, but play shows no concrete need of William's that depends on it beyond his preference.

facts.text: Dr. Uriah agreed to donate 10 gold to Father William for the Barrow Mound's upkeep; no payment has been made.

classification.stake_basis: Father William requested the 10 gold for the Barrow's upkeep and Uriah agreed, giving William a modest claim on that specific payment.

facts.text: The giant, which captured Brother Dirk on his way to the Barrow to eat him in a stew, still lives in its huge stone cottage in a forest clearing on the party's route north and endangers travellers passing near it; it is slow and was easily outrun.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: Dirk says the giant captured him and meant to eat him; capture and being eaten is a specific harm.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: Being captured and eaten means death.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: The party saw the giant and its captive and fled it; Dirk's testimony confirms it captures travellers.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: It has already captured a traveller heading the same way and still lives on the route, but nothing shows it pursuing the party now; it gave up the chase.
classification.preventability_justification: The party knows where the cottage is, can avoid the clearing, and outran the slow giant easily.
